open_points.subject: A21 security review coverage of A18
open_points.text: “after that day's changes to A01, A04, A13, A16, A17 and A18 reopened it (rule 2): every category naming them was reviewed, and no outcome and no reference changed” conflicts with the concurrency category, whose references omit A18 even though A18 defines concurrent store snapshots, non-overlapping backup runs, and reads racing backup renames and deletions.
open_points.question: Is A18 part of the concurrency review, requiring A18 and backup runs to appear in that category's references and affected subjects, or are A18's concurrency rules intentionally outside that category despite A21 defining it to cover read-check-change races and atomic transitions?
options: Add A18 to the concurrency references and backup runs to its affected subjects
State which already-referenced decision fully covers A18's concurrency behavior and why A18 itself need not be referenced
Declare A18's backup concurrency outside the concurrency category
open_points.default_guess: Add A18 to the concurrency references and list backup runs, snapshot/write races, and backup file listing/rename/delete races as affected.

witness.initial: Registry is running with service tokens shortly before 03:00 UTC while owner and service writes remain possible.
events: The backup timer starts A18's daily run and opens a read snapshot while another caller commits a store transaction.
The owner interface reads the backup listing while the run renames a temporary backup or deletes an old one.
A release reviewer follows A21's concurrency references to determine which accepted decisions establish the race and atomicity guarantees.
outcomes: A18 is treated as part of the concurrency review, so its snapshot, no-overlap, and file-race rules are traceable review evidence.
A18 is not treated as part of the concurrency review because that category does not name it, despite the newly asserted re-review of A18 changing no reference.
witness.observer: The release or security reviewer deciding whether the State 2 concurrency review is complete.
